title: Primes of a localization and the quotients by them
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in T$, $st\in T$ for $s,t\in T$), $T^{-1}A$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and $\lambda:A\to T^{-1}A$, $a\mapsto a/1$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset T^{-1}A$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Then: (1) $\mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal of $A$ with $\mathfrak p\cap T=\emptyset$, and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p\,T^{-1}A$ is the ideal of $T^{-1}A$ generated by $\lambda(\mathfrak p)$. (2) Let $\pi:A\to A/\mathfrak p$ be the quotient map and $\overline T=\pi(T)$, a multiplicative subset of the domain $A/\mathfrak p$ with $0\notin\overline T$. Then there is a unique ring isomorphism $\overline T^{-1}(A/\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}(T^{-1}A)/\mathfrak q$ sending $\pi(a)/\pi(t)$ to the class of $a/t$ ($a\in A$, $t\in T$).
